summary: AFTER the redeploy of migration d5e6f7a8b9c0, the patient WRITE path is broken: POST /api/v1/patients AND POST /api/v1/patients/register BOTH return 500 {error:{code:internal_error}} on any valid payload. Plain POST /patients worked BEFORE the redeploy (patients 83878-83881 were created earlier the same session). So this is a server-side regression introduced by the migration/redeploy, not a payload problem.

evidence.not_validation: 500 (unhandled exception), not 422 — the body passes Pydantic validation.
evidence.payload_independent: 500 reproduced with a MINIMAL body, and with patient_types sent as [] AND as null — no field combination avoids it.
evidence.frontend_status: Verified correct: right endpoints, schema-valid bodies (every field matches the generated Orval models), tsc + eslint green. Frontend now calls /patients/register with a resilient fallback to POST /patients + per-resource writes; both 500 today.

likely_backend_causes: A new column added by d5e6f7a8b9c0 is NOT NULL without a server default, so INSERT fails.
A column type mismatch (e.g. patient_types JSON) the ORM can't serialize on insert/return.
The migration was applied but the app/CRUD references a column/relationship inconsistent with the DB.
An exception in the post-insert chart_no auto-generation added to PatientCRUD.
ask: Check the backend server logs for the traceback on POST /api/v1/patients (500). The generic error envelope hides the real exception.
